hypotheses.possible_explanation: Paymentservice is part of the checkout path, so intermittent CPU throttling of paymentservice during an overlapping window could have caused checkout requests to fail as frontend.request_error events. This is a hypothesis only, not a proven cause; the clocks are not verified.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment first (resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core). Then compare the 15-second paymentservice cpu_throttle_ratio timeline cell-by-cell with the checkout error timeline across 1790630535000-1790630670000, and inspect paymentservice CPU quota/limit configuration.

hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the paymentservice deployment CPU requests/limits and cgroup throttling counters; confirm whether a non-throttled rerun changes the throttle ratio before attributing the failures to paymentservice.

caveats: Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core (evidence/7); the temporal overlap between the error burst (evidence/19) and the paymentservice throttle finding (findings/0 from evidence/15) cannot support lead/lag or causal claims until clocks are verified.

The overall sample_count (40306) and the policy-window denominator (38628) measure different scopes/windows (whole run vs run-intersection 1790630475000-1790630820000, excluding dropped leading/trailing segments); the difference is expected, not an inconsistency.

Error evidence includes only per-15s aggregate counts and 2 sample documents per group (message 'request error'); response codes and the remaining 2469 error documents were not individually inspected.
Resource summaries are interval means over 23 cells of 15s within the run-intersection window; they do not show sub-minute behavior, and zero missing/gap counts describe only the sampled grid.
Error count equality between overall and checkout (2471) is an observation, not proof that all errors originate in checkout; per-sample attribution is required.
Zero error counts after 1790630670000 and CPU means below 1 core for all measured services do not prove spare capacity or stability; they describe only the measured window.
This analysis contains no capacity bound or knee results; verdict FAIL is driven only by the error-rate policy (overall-errors) and the paymentservice cpu_throttle_ratio resource policy.

run_validity VALID and analysis_coverage COMPLETE confirm the data was accepted and retrieved; they do not cover all error causes or guarantee that the 2 sampled documents are representative (samples_per_group_limit 2).
